messages:
Falco-bot: FALCO_ALERT: possible image tampering detected — container runtime integrity alert. pod=nginx-web-abc123 namespace=frontend cluster=prod-eu-west-1 node=gke-prod-pool-1 event=filesystem_writable_mounts
Andrea: seeing this, can someone confirm if this is a false positive? :eyes:
Samir: I got the same alert. quick check: `kubectl get pod nginx-web-abc123 -n frontend -o yaml` shows hostPath mounts and privileged: true
Cheng: assigning to @SecOps Oncall. Can we cordon the node and force-delete the pod? we should capture logs first.
SecOps Oncall: on it. cordoning node now: `kubectl cordon gke-prod-pool-1` — done. grabbing container logs and node dmesg
Oliver: also snapshot the node (in GCP) and create a copy of /var/lib/docker/aufs to a forensic bucket.
Andrea: do NOT restart other pods on that node. set poddisruptionbudget overrides if needed.
Falco-bot: RELATED_ALERT: privilege escalation attempt via cap_add SYS_ADMIN on pod nginx-web-abc123
Samir: checking registry digest: `skopeo inspect docker://registry.internal.redwood.dev/frontend/nginx:latest` shows digest sha256:deadbeef
Cheng: pull image locally from registry and compute digest. compare with running container: `docker inspect --format='{{.Image}}' <container>`
Oliver: logs show the image ID on node doesn't match registry digest. suspicious.
Andrea: good catch. possible image tampering or registry compromise. Who pushed latest tag recently?
Samir: checking image push audit in Harbor: `harbor.audits` shows push by service-account:frontend-deployer@redwood-automation 03:12 UTC
Cheng: check k8s audit logs for who created pod with privileged: `kubectl logs -n kube-system audit-collector` — 03:15 request by `system:serviceaccount:frontend:deployer` from CI IP
Andrea: temporary containment: revoke token for serviceaccount frontend:deployer and remove its RBAC create permission for pods. `kubectl delete secret -n frontend frontend-deployer-token-xxxxx` and apply a deny rolebinding.
SecOps Oncall: revoked token and removed RoleBinding. confirmed no new pods created. also disabled node autoscaling to avoid rescheduling into other pools.
Oliver: we've rotated the deployer's credentials and scheduled a registry rollback to a known-good digest. notify infra to block the digest that doesn't match.
Samir: question: do we need to rotate KMS keys used for signing deployer artifacts? The deployer uses KMS-wrapped service keys stored in Vault.
Cheng: proposal: rotate the KMS key version used by deploy pipeline, invalidate old tokens, and require cosign signing with KMS plugin. low-IOC immediate action: rotate tokens, enforce image signature verification in admission controller.
Andrea: agree. add to containment -> short term: block the compromised digest in registry, rotate deployer creds, cordon & drain node, snapshot for forensics. medium term: enforce image signing, tighten RBAC for privileged pods, enable pod security admission to deny hostPath/privileged.
Falco-bot: INFO: alert correlated with suspicious outbound DNS to 54.23.12.9 from node gke-prod-pool-1
Oliver: added egress rule to block that IP and pinged network team to trace flow logs.
SecOps Oncall: containment done: node cordoned, pods evicted, registry digest blocked, deployer SA token rotated. collecting artifacts into s3://secops-forensics/1719509123/
Andrea: communication: drafting incident notice for #incidents and customer-facing status? probably internal first. @Samir can you draft? :memo:
Samir: will draft internal incident note and severity assessment. timeline: detection 03:12, containment 03:40 UTC
Cheng: post-incident actions (short list):
- enforce pod security admission (PSA) baseline->restricted for prod
- create RBAC rule to prevent creation of privileged hostPath pods by CI SAs
- require cosign signatures for images in prod and integrate KMS plugin
- increase audit log retention to 90d and centralize to BigQuery
- add registry push alerts + 2nd factor for pushing to prod repo
Oliver: also add automated digest verification at admission time: if image tag->resolve digest and compare against allowed list
Andrea: creating follow-up ticket in Security backlog and assign owners. we'll run a tabletop and full postmortem tomorrow.
SecOps Oncall: saving thread logs and artifacts. marking as incident INC-2026-045 (placeholder).
Samir: thanks everyone — ping me if you find more IOCs. :thumbsup:
Andrea: great work. we'll keep channel updated with postmortem link and next steps. :lock:
Deploy-bot: deploy blocked for repo frontend until `security/verify-image-signatures` is green
